Mongo.//: Catalog and chat storage. mongod runs as a Windows service on localhost only. The pre-launch data is preserved under 'wajibat_test'.

Https.//: Public endpoint for the shop till (LocalHandler). Loads the live orderorange SAN certificate straight from IIS's WebHosting store (its private key is non-exportable, so it can't be copied to a .pfx). A client reaching https://orderorange.com:8500 validates cleanly; on certificate renewal, restart the API to pick up the new one.

InternalHttps.//: Loopback for the IIS web apps and the api.orderorange.com proxy. TLS even on 127.0.0.1 (Majed, 2026-09-02: stop all http). Self-signed CN=oo-loopback (SAN localhost + 127.0.0.1) in LocalMachine\My, trusted machine-wide via LocalMachine\Root; recreate with New-SelfSignedCertificate if it ever expires (2031). Staging deploys rewrite the port to 8620.

Seed.//: Production: create the schema and nothing else — no invented stores, customers or order history. Use 'Demo' or omit for a populated development world. The pre-launch data lives in OrderOrangeTest.

ConnectionStrings.//: The live production database. Everything from before launch was renamed to OrderOrangeTest and is still there, untouched.

Google.//: OAuth client id from Google Cloud Console -> Credentials -> OAuth client ID (Web application). Public by design: it is served to the browser. Leave empty to hide the Google button in all four apps.

Smtp.//: Sends the one-time sign-in code. For Google Workspace: Host smtp.gmail.com, Port 587, User the full mailbox address, Password a 16-character APP PASSWORD (Google refuses the normal account password for SMTP). Empty Host = email sign-in is reported as unavailable rather than silently failing.

Auth.//: Password sign-in was removed from every screen; this keeps the endpoint reachable as a way back in if Google and email both fail. Set to false to close it permanently.

Admin.//: Only these emails may sign in as an Administrator, whatever the method (Google, email code, password). Comma-separated. Empty = no restriction.

Media.//: The API's PUBLIC origin, used to hand out image URLs (api/media/*) instead of inline base64 on customer payloads — a store page went from 1.4 MB to ~0.2 MB. Remove the key and everything flows inline again. Must be a hostname Cloudflare proxies on 443: orderorange.com:8500 died the day the apex went behind the orange cloud (2026-09-02, every store image broke). Staging has no proxied hostname and simply drops the key.

Suggested.//: Shops the customer home puts forward in its 'Suggested' strip, in this order. Real, hand-onboarded stores — the generated catalog is not advertised. Empty list hides the strip entirely. Mixed store types are fine: the home page shows only the ones matching the vertical being browsed, so a Shop appears under Shops and a Restaurant under Food.
Suggested.//order: Newest first after Shirin Bano. About six cards fit before the strip needs scrolling, so anything featured past the sixth is effectively invisible — put newly onboarded shops near the front, not at the end.

Home.//: The customer home hides dishes priced below this (OMR) — auto-created Water, bags, sauces. Store pages still show everything.

Seo.//: Which shops /sitemap.xml offers Google. RealStoreMinId keeps the generated catalog out of it. SitemapMinMenuItems keeps half-onboarded shops out: registering a shop auto-creates one Water item, so a bar of 'any dish at all' let empty shops through and risked a thin-content mark on the domain.

Jwt.//: Key, issuer and audience keep their original values on purpose — changing any of them invalidates every signed-in session on the day of the switch.
